<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תמוז_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518919340_theRebbe_24" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_9E_D7_95_D7_96_meluket__BH_POST_1766518919340_theRebbe_24__p007">
  <section v="18">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the connection between reviewing one's chapter one hundred and one times and the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy, where the one hundred and first study elevates the previous hundred studies into a form of service.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And one may add in explanation of the connection of the one who reviews his chapter one hundred and one times</t>
    <t s="1">(the effort of changing nature and habit in the study of Torah)</t>
    <t s="2">to the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy,</t>
    <t s="3">for through the study on the one hundred and first time,</t>
    <t s="4">even the study of the one hundred times prior is in a manner of service.</t>
    <t s="5">In the analogy of what was explained above</t>
    <t s="6">(section 5)</t>
    <t s="7">regarding the number thirteen,</t>
    <t s="8">that through the addition of the one,</t>
    <t s="9">an elevation occurs</t>
    <t s="10">(a change or at least an addition)</t>
    <t s="11">in the twelve.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="19">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that Moshe's prayer mentioning the name "E-l" alludes to the drawing down of the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy through prayer, which then extends into Torah study.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">9)</t>
    <t s="1">And based on this, one may explain that in the teaching of the Maggid of Mezeritch cited in the maamar above, that when Moshe mentioned the name "E-l"</t>
    <t s="2">(the first attribute of the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy)</t>
    <t s="3">the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him a kal vachomer</t>
    <t s="4">(the first of the thirteen principles by which the Torah is expounded),</t>
    <t s="5">it is precise that Moshe in his prayer said "E-l, please heal her, please."</t>
    <t s="6">For one may say,</t>
    <t s="7">that the precision in his prayer is to hint that the primary drawing down of the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy that are above the chain of descent is through prayer,</t>
    <t s="8">and through this the drawing down comes afterward also in Torah.</t>
    <t s="9">And this is also the reason that the matter of drawing down not according to the measure of the elevation through Torah</t>
    <t s="10">(of many)</t>
    <t s="11">is learned from the drawing down through prayer</t>
    <t s="12">(of many),</t>
    <t s="13">for the essence</t>
    <t s="14">(and source)</t>
    <t s="15">of this matter is in prayer,</t>
    <t s="16">and through this it is drawn afterward also in Torah.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="20">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section notes that the principle of prayer preceding Torah is hinted at in two chapters of Tehillim related to the birthday of the Baal HaGeulah in this year.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And to add58,</t>
    <t s="1">that this matter</t>
    <t s="2">(that through prayer it is drawn afterward also in Torah)</t>
    <t s="3">is also hinted at in the two chapters of Tehillim that pertain to the birthday59</t>
    <t s="4">of the Baal HaGeulah in this year.</t>
    <t s="5">For in Psalm 102</t>
    <t s="6">[which relates to the conclusion of the year 102]</t>
    <t s="7">it begins with "A prayer of the afflicted" etc., and later in the psalm it says "This shall be written for the last generation" etc.60</t>
    <t s="8">which refers to the Torah, which is eternal.</t>
    <t s="9">And similarly in Psalm 103</t>
    <t s="10">[which relates to the year 103,</t>
    <t s="11">beginning from the birthday]</t>
    <t s="12">which begins "Bless the L-rd, O my soul," which is a prayer of praise and thanksgiving,</t>
    <t s="13">and later in the psalm it says "Bless the L-rd, you His angels, mighty in strength, who do His word, to hearken to the voice of His word"61,</t>
    <t s="14">first "who do" and then "to hearken"62,</t>
    <t s="15">the precedence of "we will do" to "we will hear," which was the preparation for receiving the Torah.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
